estimate.question: What do I need to start an estimate?
estimate.answer: Start with your home's location and an initial system size. SolarDream uses regional sunlight to show a first estimate, then you can add usage details when you are ready.

quote.question: Are these numbers a final quote?
quote.answer: No. They are an early planning estimate. An engineer reviews the roof, equipment, and household usage before preparing an official proposal.

bill.question: Do I need an electricity bill first?
bill.answer: No. You can explore your home's potential first. If you have a bill, sharing it later helps us shape the system around real usage.

size.question: Can I choose the system size myself?
size.answer: Yes. Move the system slider or choose a common size to see the estimate update, then review the choice against your roof and usage.

next.question: What happens after the estimate?
next.answer: Continue with the design flow or speak with an engineer. We review the information, arrange a site assessment, and explain the next step before you commit.

accuracy.question: How accurate is the solar estimate?
accuracy.answer: It is a planning estimate based on regional sunlight and system efficiency. Roof direction, shading, equipment, tariff, and actual weather can change the final result.

PrivacyPolicy.title: Privacy Policy
PrivacyPolicy.defaultContent:
Privacy Policy

Last updated: July 18, 2026

SolarDream Platform prioritizes your privacy. This policy explains how we collect, use, and protect your personal information when you access our website and solar system estimation services.

1. Information We Collect

We collect personal information only to the extent necessary to provide our services, including:

  • Account Data: When you log in via Google or LINE, the system collects basic information with your consent from that platform, such as your first and last name, email address, and profile picture.
  • Service Data: Electricity bill information, electricity consumption behavior, location coordinates (to evaluate sunlight potential), and related details used to generate quotations.
  • Analytics Data: Website usage statistics, browser type, and device information used to access the site.

2. Use of Cookies and Analytics

We use cookies and similar tracking technologies to improve your user experience:

  • Strictly Necessary Cookies: Used for remembering login status (session) and account security. These cannot be disabled.
  • Umami Analytics: We use Umami to collect anonymous website traffic statistics (privacy-focused analytics) to analyze platform performance.
  • Your Right to Manage Cookies: You have the full right to accept or decline the use of non-essential cookies and analytics tracking at any time via the cookie banner or the "Privacy Settings" menu on your profile page.

3. Use and Disclosure of Information

Your information will be used to:

  • Create profiles, generate quotations, and track the progress of your solar installation project.
  • Communicate, send document status notifications, or send newsletters (in case you opt-in to receive news).

We do not sell or rent your personal information to third parties. Information may only be shared with engineers or partners involved in your system installation.

4. Data Subject Rights

Under the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA), you have the right to take the following actions through the system settings menu:

  • Right to Access: You can request to download the information recorded in the system.
  • Right to be Forgotten (Deletion): You can request to delete your account. The system will anonymize your identity data but will retain the statistical solar system data for system bookkeeping completeness as required by law.

5. Contact Us

If you have any questions regarding this Privacy Policy, you can contact us via the Support Desk channel on the SolarDream platform.

SupportKnowledge.intro: Start with safe, verifiable checks. If something still looks wrong, send a service request with supporting photos.
SupportKnowledge.safetyTitle: Do not open equipment covers yourself
SupportKnowledge.safetyDescription: DC equipment can retain voltage even after a breaker is off. If you notice a burning smell, unusual sound, or excessive heat, keep clear and contact our service team.

inverter.question: What should I do when the inverter shows a red light?
inverter.answer: Record the error code and take a photo. Check whether the AC/DC breakers are ON. If the red light remains, do not open the unit; shut the system down according to its guide and submit a service request.

bill.question: How do I read a PEA bill to understand savings?
bill.answer: Compare kWh consumption with the same month last year, allowing for the billing-period length. A lower bill may not equal total solar production because solar energy is used in the home first.

production.question: Why is the system producing less than usual?
production.answer: Weather, shade, dust, temperature, and inverter downtime can all affect output. Compare similar weather and time periods; if output is down over 20% for several days, save the graph and contact service.

cleaning.question: How often should solar panels be cleaned?
cleaning.answer: Inspect and clean every six months, or earlier in dusty areas, near construction, or where bird droppings collect. Avoid hot panels and harsh chemicals.

outage.question: Why does solar stop during a power outage?
outage.answer: Standard on-grid systems stop exporting automatically when the grid is down to protect utility workers. They resume after grid power returns and the inverter completes its checks.
